items.name: SDN Epoch State
items.what: TLE-to-numerical handoff (Evidence-Supported ASO Catalog, section 5): evaluates each $MPE element set with SGP4 at zero elapsed time, transforms the TEME state to GCRF at the same instant (IAU 2006/2000A via ERFA, velocity including the frame rotation rate), verifies the round trip, and emits one single-row $OEM per element set with its lineage and initial-condition uncertainty marked unknown. Pure compute; output bytes depend only on input bytes.

items.name: Measurement-based Orbit Estimation
items.what: Measurement-based Orbit Estimation: Analysis module

items.name: GP prediction-error model
items.what: Empirical SGP4 prediction error by orbit regime and prediction age, in RTN. Element sets are propagated to later element sets of the same object (consecutive-set differences, which are not truth) or to independent reference states (GCRF, from analysis/reference-states). Batches accumulate counts, moments and histograms; finalize gives mean, covariance, quantiles, robust sigma and clipped covariance per stratum. With a model on accumulate (reference mode), each error is also tested against its stratum's model covariance (Mahalanobis d^2 against chi-square with 3 degrees of freedom, every sample counted) and finalize gates each stratum CALIBRATED, FAILED or INSUFFICIENT; scale_model fits per-stratum scale factors to reference-state errors. screening_evaluation scores a probabilistic (Foster Pc), a bounded-set and a possibility (admissible-set) screening rule on independent cases built from reference-state errors with synthetic true misses. hpop_arcs and hpop_coverage calibrate HPOP covariance (P0 at the element-set epoch, white-acceleration process noise) against reference states.

items.name: Launch collision avoidance screening
items.what: Screens a launch window: every liftoff time on a grid, every launched segment against every orbiting object, spherical or radial/in-track/cross-track ellipsoid criteria per object class. Returns prohibited liftoff spans and the worst approach of each run.

items.name: Launch trajectory tracking and projected insertion
items.what: Reconstructs a launch ascent from altitude and speed telemetry (ground track, downrange, flight-path angle, instantaneous impact point, each sample's osculating apsides, and the insertion orbit at engine cutoff), and projects the insertion orbit of a scheduled launch from its pad, liftoff time, target orbit and a comparable flight's profile, including the liftoff times that join a reference plane.

items.name: Maneuver detection
items.what: Detects maneuvers in an element-set history. Takes each element set's trajectory from any propagator, finds where consecutive trajectories cross, measures the energy and orbit-plane change there, and flags steps beyond the object's own noise. Emits $MNV DETECTED events with time, in-track and cross-track delta-V, pre and post states and characterization.

items.name: Milky Way model
items.what: The Milky Way's SDSS r, g and i starlight and dust baked in C++ WASM from published models (Juric 2008, Flynn 2006, Robin 2003, Drimmel & Spergel 2001, Reid 2019, Wegg & Gerhard 2013, Portail 2017, Bland-Hawthorn & Gerhard 2016; colors by Riello et al. 2021), drawn as SDSS gri composites are (Lupton et al. 2004, fitted to SkyServer), with the local 3D dust map of Edenhofer et al. 2024 loaded from its SDN publication.

items.name: Observation simulator
items.what: Simulates raw sensor observations of targets from their truth trajectories: radar ($RDO), optical ($EOO) and passive RF ($RFO), scheduled inside access windows with tasking limits, measured with the estimation module's models in GCRF, with noise, biases, detection limits and false alarms.

items.name: Named Parameter Catalog
items.what: Evaluates named calculation parameters on orbital states: the classical and equinoctial element sets, the derived orbit scalars, the angular-momentum triple, the B-plane and asymptote sets, the planet-relative angles, the atomic and dynamical time scales and the state-transition sub-matrices, over the shared IAU-2006/2000A chain. Publishes its own roster as an SDS PCE catalog, including the parameters it declares and refuses.

items.name: Private screening decoys
items.what: Decoy orbits for private conjunction screening and the experiment that measures how well they hide a real orbit. decoys generates decoy histories from a population of real ones (independent draws, rotated copies, resampled or chained histories, or copies of the target itself). features computes rotation-invariant features of each history from its element sets (gp view) or from daily HPOP ephemeris windows (hpop view), including the distance to the nearest public object. distinguish trains a gradient-boosted tree classifier, cross-validated by target, and reports AUC, a 95 % lower bound on epsilon, and the probability that the real history scores highest of N.

items.name: Reference states
items.what: Independent reference states for calibrating orbit uncertainty: precise orbits read from SP3 (files/orbit-products) become GCRF/UTC states per catalogued object, with the product's stated accuracy as covariance and its provenance.

items.name: RPO history
items.what: Relative-motion history of a pair of objects in WASM: curvilinear RIC/RTN relative states from element-set histories propagated by epoch-state, maneuvers from maneuver-detection, and inspection geometry (solar phase angle, eclipses, line of sight, illumination, sensor beam membership), emitted as SDS $OCM/$CVR/$MNV records.

items.name: CelesTrak Reference Nodes
items.what: Request-builder and parser flow nodes for the CelesTrak reference lanes: gp_groups turns a timer tick into one hostcap/http-request frame per GP group query (47 GROUP tokens plus the gpz / gpz-plus SPECIAL queries, overridable via node CONFIG celestrak_gp_groups) and ONE job frame carrying the ordered group list; parse_gp_groups pairs the responses with that list by ordinal and emits one $EGP (Entity Group, QUERY_SNAPSHOT membership over the group's OMM rows) per group, with the concatenated payloads as the raw archive and an 'unchanged' frame for groups that answered 304. satcat_reference emits the launch-site and owner/source table fetches; parse_satcat_reference reads those HTML tables into $SIT rows (launch sites) and $LCC rows (legacy owner codes, matched strictly against the generated enum; unknown codes become provenance warnings and are skipped). Every job carries origin_id celestrak.org, origin_name CelesTrak, dataset_id and the licence terms (node CONFIG celestrak_license / celestrak_license_url / celestrak_citation override the defaults), and every ingest meta carries the same attribution plus the wasm-authored provenance JSON. The job is one frame for all groups because the compiled flow runtime hands a node at most 64 frames per invocation; the group list is capped at 63 for the same reason. No capabilities: plugin.getConfig is a builtin and this module performs no I/O of its own.

items.name: Cellular Base-Station Aggregation Nodes
items.what: Many cellular/base-station registries -> one deconflicted SDS $TBS site stream. Three pure flow nodes: `route` turns one $HTQ request into N hostcap/http-request GET descriptors for the provider set the CALLER named plus the run contract; `parse` decodes each provider native payload into normalized reports; `deconflict` merges reports across providers under the caller chosen tbsMergeMethod and emits a size-prefixed $TBS record stream plus a run summary. Configuration is REQUEST-SCOPED, never node-global, so two callers can ask for different provider sets at once without either changing what the node is. NO CAPABILITIES, deliberately: this plugin performs no I/O — http is the generic hostcap connector node, and the credential lane (keyslot.unwrap + secrets.put/clear) is a SEPARATE wasmedge-only plugin, cell-tower-credentials, so the grants an operator makes for credentials never attach to the code that parses provider bodies and stays browser-testable.

items.name: SDN GP Archive Records
items.what: Builds the GP history archive's $MPE element sets and $CAT catalog rows in archive encoding v1: the exact byte layout the archive's content IDs (sha256 over the record bytes) depend on. Records are built with the schema-generated SDS C++ builders; field names and vtable slots come only from the generated headers, and the field order and default handling are a compatibility contract gated by fixture bytes from the importer's original builder. Pure compute; output bytes depend only on input bytes.

items.name: M-Lab Starlink Connectivity Source Nodes
items.what: M-Lab NDT statistics pipeline -> SDS $CNP constellation-network-performance records. Two pure flow nodes: `request` turns a cron timer tick into ONE whole-file hostcap/http-request GET of https://statistics.measurementlab.net/v0/asn/<ASN>/<YEAR>/histogram_daily_stats.json (anonymous HTTPS, no BigQuery, no auth) plus the parser attribution job; `parse` joins that job with the http response, collapses the eight per-date log-bucket rows into one aggregate per UTC day and emits a size-prefixed $CNP record stream for hostcap/storage-ingest. Starlink IS the client-ASN key: the upstream query groups by client.Network.ASNumber and AS14593 is SPACEX-STARLINK, so no constellation is ever inferred from a throughput number. A quantity exists only as a CNPMetric with UNITS and PROVENANCE, and CNPMetric has no scalar VALUE: throughput publishes six CNPStatistic entries (MINIMUM, PERCENTILE 25, MEDIAN, MEAN, PERCENTILE 75, MAXIMUM) in Mbps verbatim and minimum-RTT publishes exactly one MEDIAN in ms. REGION is omitted entirely because the per-ASN export carries no geographic key. M-Lab test data is CC0, so every metric carries LICENSE CC0-1.0, M-Lab's own citation in ATTRIBUTION and NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY false. No capabilities: this node performs no I/O — http and storage are the generic hostcap connector nodes. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted on the parse node: the method emits a single notice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced.

items.name: SatNOGS DB RF Transmitter Source Nodes
items.what: SatNOGS DB (Libre Space Foundation) -> SDS $RFB transmitter records. Two pure flow nodes: `request` turns a cron timer tick into ONE whole-table hostcap/http-request GET of https://db.satnogs.org/api/transmitters/?format=json (bulk, never a pagination walk — the source-policy.json crawl ruling) plus the parser attribution job; `parse` joins that job with the http response, decodes ~4,994 transmitter rows and emits a size-prefixed $RFB record stream for hostcap/storage-ingest. One $RFB record carries exactly one LINK_DIRECTION, so a Transceiver/Transponder becomes an UPLINK + DOWNLINK pair sharing ID_TRANSMITTER (the SatNOGS uuid). SatNOGS publishes HERTZ; every frequency field written is MHz per the normative RFB units rule. Licence is CC-BY-SA-4.0: every record carries CITATION verbatim and the batch provenance carries license/license_url/citation so the share-alike obligation survives republication. No capabilities: this node performs no I/O — http and storage are the generic hostcap connector nodes. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted, never treated as a failed fetch: the parse method emits a single notice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced.

items.name: SigMF Raw-IQ Capture Source Nodes
items.what: Public raw-IQ archives -> SDS $IQC pointer records. Two pure flow nodes: `request` turns a cron timer tick into ONE bulk hostcap/http-request GET of the configured archive's metadata index (default IQEngine: https://www.iqengine.org/api/datasources/local/local/meta, anonymous, no token, ~31 MB, 36,636 SigMF documents) plus the parser attribution job naming the source adapter; `parse` joins that job with the response, decodes each SigMF document and emits a size-prefixed $IQC record stream for hostcap/storage-ingest. $IQC IS A POINTER RECORD: it carries where the samples are (PAYLOADS[].URL), what they hash to (BYTE_SHA512 from SigMF core:sha512) and nothing else — CUSTODY stays UPSTREAM_ONLY and no payload is ever mirrored. SigMF publishes HERTZ, so SAMPLE_RATE_HZ / CENTER_FREQ_HZ / FREQ_*_EDGE_HZ carry the value unconverted ($RFB's MHz convention is deliberately NOT adopted) and DATATYPE is the SigMF token verbatim. GEOLOCATION is omitted entirely when the source published no position, and a transposed lat/lon is refused rather than swapped. LICENCE IS PER RECORDING: core:license rides verbatim and an absent one means UNKNOWN TERMS, never public domain. The source-adapter registry ships exactly one adapter, the one whose anonymous read surface was verified live; a stub adapter that fabricates data is forbidden and an unknown adapter id fails closed. No capabilities: this node performs no I/O — http and storage are the generic hostcap connector nodes. HTTP 304 Not Modified is accepted, never treated as a failed fetch: the parse method emits a single notice on its 'unchanged' port and nothing else, so no batch is stored or announced.

items.name: Global Ensemble Forecast Parser Nodes
items.what: Pure WASM parser flow nodes for a machine-learned global ensemble weather forecast source: parse_cloud_chunks joins the request-builder's per-chunk job JSON (one per Zarr v3 chunk of a cloud-cover array) with the matching hostcap/http-request responses POSITIONALLY (job k <-> response k), decodes each chunk through its declared codec chain (bytes float32/float16 in this build; a zstd stage reports codec-unsupported until a decoder is vendored), validates the byte length against the declared chunk shape, and emits one size-prefixed $WXF tile per chunk (own GRID, TILE_INDEX/TILE_COUNT over the declared global grid, VALUE_MIN/VALUE_MAX/MISSING_COUNT, licence class copied from the job) plus the storage.ingest_with_source meta (batch = sha256 of the concatenated chunk bodies, licence-bearing provenance). parse_cyclone_tracks turns the tropical-cyclone track CSV into one $TCT record per (storm, member) with points sorted by valid time, knots/hPa/nautical-mile source units converted exactly to m/s, Pa and km, wind radii at 34/50/64 kt by quadrant and the intensity category from maximum sustained wind; it emits the meta, the record stream and the raw CSV for archiving. Records are built with the spacedatastandards.org GENERATED C++ code. No capabilities: this node performs no I/O. Nothing about the upstream bucket layout is hardcoded — chunk shape, codecs, dimension order, dtype and grid arrive on the job JSON and are validated by size, because the store is allow-listed and its layout could not be verified anonymously.

items.name: vCard Projection
items.what: Pure WASM vCard 3.0 projection of $EPM (§21 literal-key): card_full (full contact card + verification chain + photo), card_compact (QR-density card: sign/encrypt/epmsig only), card_parse (vCard → EPM fields). No capabilities: this module performs no I/O, no signing, no key derivation — it projects record bytes to text.

items.name: CCSDS Message Reader
items.what: Reads and writes the two CCSDS keyword-value messages this stack round-trips — the Attitude Ephemeris Message (504.0-B-2) and the Tracking Data Message (503.0-B-2 Cor.1) — and projects them onto SDS $AEM and $TDM with the file-level facts carried out separately as $NCD. Parsing goes through an ordered keyword/value/units/comment document rather than a struct, so a keyword the record has no field for is still read, and the projection NAMES what it cannot carry instead of dropping it in silence. $AEM always takes the verbose ATTITUDE_DATA_LINES form with an explicit per-state EPOCH: the published Figure G-4 steps 2336.3 s then 1.0 s then 98398.0 s, so the compact START_TIME + i * STEP_SIZE array cannot express a real AEM at all, and a record that arrives in that form is refused rather than guessed at because rebuilding its epochs needs a leap-second table this module does not carry. $TDM observations are per-observation (KEYWORD, EPOCH, VALUE) triples in file order, never sorted, deduplicated or laid on a grid: published Figure E-17 stamps its last RCS observation 0.2678 s EARLIER than the line above it. TRANSMIT_RAMPS is left absent rather than empty, so a ramp-free record is exactly a CCSDS-conformant TDM. No time-scale conversion happens here; epochs stay the text the file wrote. A malformed message is a named status, never a trap and never a NaN. Pure compute — no capabilities, no host calls, no filesystem.

items.name: Orbit Products Reader
items.what: Reads the four ephemeris CONTAINERS this stack round-trips — SPK (NAIF DAF, segment types 8, 9 and 13), SP3-c/d, Code-500 and scenario-epoch STK ephemeris — plus CCSDS-OEM keyword-value notation, and projects them onto SDS $OEM with the container's own facts carried out separately as $NCD. A container is a wire format, not a standard: the state history becomes $OEM and the file-level header, comment area, segment address ranges and accuracy block become the native-container descriptor, so a read-then-write cycle reproduces the source instead of inventing header values. Each container is evaluated by the interpolation rule it declares, never by a rule this module picked, and no time-scale conversion happens here: epochs stay on the scale the container named and that name is carried out with them. A malformed container is a named status, never a trap and never a NaN. Converts public-format Vimpel osculating element tables to analytic J2000 epoch OPM states with source provenance; no differenced velocity or covariance is invented. Converts SP Vector/Covariance Messages, legacy V2.0 text or superseded $VCM records, to $OCM without deriving uncertainty or splitting the ballistic coefficient.

items.name: Event Locator
items.what: Locates events on a supplied trajectory as roots of a continuous event function: eclipse umbra, penumbra and antumbra, station contact with light-time correction, body intrusion into a conic field of view, apsides, node crossings and a stopping condition on any named catalog parameter. One bracketing scan and one Brent refinement serve every class, so the located epoch does not depend on the scan step. The trajectory arrives as a port; this module carries no propagator. Locates composed access-constraint windows from SDS ACW requests through the shared C++ access evaluator.
